last_summary: Replication Seeder run 1 (gear 1, `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `letta model get` @06:06:21Z — no quota error, no gear-2). +4 artifacts, all read from primary sources in the corpus rather than from citations: 3 validations + 1 dossier. (1) LENR/transmutation — Osaka University (Higashiyama, Miyamaru, Takahashi) with an MHI co-author ran MHI's D2-permeation Cs→Pr experiment three times and reported Pr from all three runs, confirmed by ICP-MS *and* 14 MeV NAA at JAERI-FNS; filed **medium**, and the load-bearing caveat is that MHI (the claimant) fabricated and supplied the samples, ran the ICP-MS, and permeated the NAA sample — vendor material plus a vendor co-author is not third-party replication; NAA rests on two data points, >50% error bars, apparent half-life ~50d vs 32.5d exact; the model's own predicted 4He is listed as future work. (2) LENR/glow-discharge radiation — Cantwell & McConnell (Coolescence LLC, 2008) partially replicated Storms/Scanlan's glow-discharge radiation and then *removed the anomaly*: CR-39 no tracks, Si detector no counts, magnetic deflector (calibrated on 14C betas, 50%/80% reduction at 1/2 A) no effect, and the counts are indifferent to deuterium and to palladium — verdict `consistent with conventionally produced low-energy x-rays`, `if any anomalous radiation was produced it was below the sensitivity threshold`; the claim's headline monoenergetic ~0.8 MeV electrons are a direct negative. Filed **medium-high** — a normalizing partial replication. (3) NEW DOMAIN water electrolysis — Dave Lawton's 2006 build of Stanley Meyer's demonstration electrolyser (six 316L concentric tube pairs, 1–2 mm gap, 5 in, tap water with no additives, two-NE555 gated pulse + BUZ350 MOSFET, bifilar ferrite inductors), documented by Patrick J. Kelly in `A Practical Guide to 'Free Energy' Devices` Part D14: 'an impressive rate of electrolysis', circuits 'assessed as operating at about 300% of the Faraday assumed maximum efficiency', current per added tube falling (1 A → <0.5 A → <2 A at three → ~100 mA each for 4th/5th → ~0 for 6th). Filed **low** — the 300% is asserted and not derived, no gas volume against charge, no stated Faraday baseline, no drying step, no uncertainty. (4) Dossier 052 — Meyer resonant water electrolysis, tier straw ~$200-350, `protocol ready`, built around the one design decision the lineage never made: **dry the gas, count the coulombs**, with the Faraday baseline stated in the dossier (190.2 uL/C total H2+O2 at 25C/1 atm dry; rig gate 90-110% of that on the plain-DC control) and the vapour/mist artefact named as the boring explanation before anyone spends money. NO DUPLICATION: checked all 33 validations / 57 dossiers / 50 quests first — LaB6 glow-discharge, Hylenr-TAMU, He-3 nanocomposites, Schauberger CFD, magneto-culture and biodynamic were already filed; these three are new, none re-files them. MINED where the mass actually is: the corpus index shards hold 427+ title-level replication documents (mostly lenr-canr.org, ids 1497630-1498105), and the three artifacts were read in full from PDFs at tuks.nl and lenr-canr.org, so every claim above traces to a URL and a corpus record id. ROTATION NOTE for next run: two of three validations lean LENR (8 of 36 now LENR-family — the 6 pre-existing `lenr-*` files plus today's Iwamura and Cantwell) — rotate to acoustic resonance, radionics, water structuring or electromedicine circuits. CORRECTION, same run: an earlier draft of this line read `7 of 37`; that was an arithmetical error by me (33 + 3 = 36). Counted, not assumed — the contents API lists 36 files in `synthesis/validations/` at ref=main, 8 of them `lenr-*`. Both figures corrected in the follow-up commit rather than quietly restated. FEED: not rebuilt locally — `library_feed.json` is cron-owned and a rebuild from this sandbox is the documented feed-gutting failure mode; the hourly bake folds in every file in the three Yard subdirs (measured end-to-end 09-25, 24→27), so verification is a post-bake read, not a local build. SETUP: init+fetch --depth 1 --filter=blob:none (1.15s) + HTTP reads, no working tree, no sparse-cone risk; push via plumbing by SHA.
